description: This bar chart illustrates the mean effect sizes for six different multilingual BERT models—mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂—across four morphosyntactic tagging categories: case, gender, number, and tense. The horizontal axis is labeled “tag” and displays these four categories in left-to-right order. The vertical axis is labeled “effect” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20, with tick marks at intervals of 5. Each category on the horizontal axis contains a group of six bars, one for each model, with the bars colored according to a legend in the top right corner: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). Error bars extend vertically from each bar, indicating the standard error of the mean. For the “case” category, the mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ bars are the tallest, reaching approximately 12 and 11 respectively, while the mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂ bars are the shortest, around 6. In the “gender” category, the mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ bars are again the tallest at approximately 4.5, followed by mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂ at about 3.5, with the other models showing smaller effects. For “number,” all bars are relatively low, with values clustered near zero, though the mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ bars are slightly higher at around 2.5. In the “tense” category, all bars are very short, with values mostly below 1, and the mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ bars are slightly above zero. The bars are not sorted; they are presented in the order specified by the legend, with each group of six bars corresponding to a specific tag category. No bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding and error bars.
